Thoroughness: very thorough. Read each listed file IN FULL (use Read with no limit).

SCOPE — the customer DOMAINS / SSL / BUSINESS EMAIL / WEBMAIL cluster:
Routes:
- /opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/domains/page.tsx
- /opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/domains/[id]/page.tsx

Components (/opt/nxeon/components/customer/): DomainSearch.tsx, DomainRegisterWizard.tsx, DomainTransferIn.tsx, DomainTransferInWizard.tsx, DomainIdeaGenerator.tsx, DomainControls.tsx, DomainChecklist.tsx, DnsQuickSetup.tsx, DomainAdvanced.tsx, DomainRedirects.tsx, EmailDnsSetup.tsx, EmailHosting.tsx (1440 lines), SslCertificates.tsx, SslManager.tsx, CloudflareConnect.tsx, CloudflareIntegration.tsx, and the whole /opt/nxeon/components/customer/mail/ folder (MailClient.tsx 912, MailSettings.tsx 1755, Composer.tsx 928, ComposeProvider, ContactPanel, FolderRail, MessageList, ReadingPane, ShortcutHelp, util.tsx, recipients.ts).
Also grep app/api for routes under /api/mail, /api/domains, /api/dns, /api/email to know what the client components fetch.

DELIVER, with file:line citations:
1. For EACH route: purpose; `dynamic`/`revalidate`; server vs client split; data loaded (Prisma models, lib functions, server actions, API routes); primary user actions; TAB/segment list and implementation (URL param? state? which component); every modal/drawer/wizard/confirm it can open (name, trigger, purpose); content width/layout (full-bleed? max-w? grid? — the mail page is full-bleed per Shell.tsx — confirm and describe its internal 3-pane layout); header pattern (PortalHero variant / PageHeader / custom); loading/empty/error states present.
2. /dashboard/domains/[id] specifically: enumerate EVERY card/section in render order with the component that renders it and any show/hide conditions (e.g. registered-here vs external domain, Cloudflare-connected, has hosting, has email). For each section list the actions inside (buttons, forms, toggles) and the server-action / API they call. This page is called out in the redesign brief as "the clearest example of the accumulated-design problem" so be meticulous.
3. DnsQuickSetup: what "quick setup" tasks/templates exist (website connect, Google Workspace, M365, Nxeon email, SPF/DKIM/DMARC, verification, etc.), and how the DNS record table works (columns, inline edit? drawer? add/edit/delete/duplicate?).
4. DomainRegisterWizard + DomainSearch + DomainTransferInWizard: step lists, fields, pay CTA, post-payment target, TLD suggestions, pricing display (registration vs renewal), WHOIS privacy option.
5. EmailHosting.tsx: this is the "Mailboxes" page — enumerate its sections, the subscription/plan model (how do you buy email, per mailbox or per plan?), mailbox CRUD actions, aliases, forwarding, DNS verification (SPF/DKIM/DMARC) states, password reset, quota, and every modal.
6. The webmail (/dashboard/mail + mail/*): layout (folder rail / message list / reading pane), the compose flow (ComposeProvider mounted in Shell), settings (MailSettings tabs list), contacts, keyboard shortcuts, which API routes it uses. Note how "Inbox" (webmail) vs "Mailboxes" (management) are separated and any cross-links between them.
7. SSL page: what certificates are listed (VPS websites? hosting? domains?), actions (issue/renew/upload?), and how SslCertificates vs SslManager differ.
8. Terminology inconsistencies (e.g. "Business email" vs "Mailboxes" vs "Email hosting" vs "Mail"; "Connect" vs "Link" vs "Attach"; "Register" vs "Buy" vs "Search") and structural inconsistencies vs the servers area (different header component, different tab style, different card density).
Be exhaustive — this is the "no functionality gets lost" safety net for a redesign.
